Mississippi Sound and Bight Food Web Challenge

Build populations from the bottom up, then see which populations can feed — and which become food.

Population rule: Environmental stress is applied first, then feeding and predation occur. Producers can supply up to 2 grazing units per population, but stressful salinity or temperature can reduce production. Surviving populations carry forward to the next measured year.

Choose Your Food Web Activity

Explore a Mississippi Sound and Bight food web in two different ways.

Full Food Web Game

Build your ecosystem over 10 rounds using measured salinity and temperature conditions from 2011–2020. Keep populations alive, maintain diversity, and support a connected food web to earn points.

Temperature & Salinity Investigation

Build one food web, choose salinity and temperature from 0–40, and investigate how environmental exposure, feeding, and predation change the community. Rerun the same web under different conditions.

Game Instructions

At the start of every round, add five groups of organisms to your food web. Click the plus sign next to a group to add one population unit and the minus sign to remove a population unit. The plus sign will turn gray when you cannot add any more groups. Make sure to add enough food for your predators by looking at what your animals eat. When you have your food web built, click the Run Round button to earn points and then scroll down the page to see which organisms survived the year and which ones did not.
